answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a cedar as the anchor of the cost.
